headline: NORTHERN STAR Doubles Alaska Gold Hoard: Pogo Mine Hits 9.3Moz — Reserves Jump 10% to 2.39Moz
snippet: Northern Star (ASX:NST) released a sweeping resource update showing its Pogo mine in Alaska now hosts 9.3 million oz of gold at 7.6 g/t — more than doubling measured, indicated, and inferred tonnage year-over-year. Proven and probable reserves rose 10% to 2.39Moz at 6.7 g/t, driven by the maiden Star deposit and deep drilling at South Pogo and East Deeps. NST shares surged 8% on the initial ASX announcement.

headline: COPPER STUMBLES Below $14,000 as Traders Brace for June 30 US Tariff Decision
snippet: LME copper fell through $14,000/t on June 4 as investors de-risked ahead of the June 30 deadline when the US Commerce Secretary must deliver a refined copper tariff recommendation to President Trump. Goldman Sachs' base case is a 25%+ duty starting 2027; US monthly copper import volumes had already surged to 150,000–200,000 tonnes during the pre-tariff arbitrage window.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Locks In $1.6B in Federal Funds — $3.5B War Chest for Mine-to-Magnet Build-Out
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) executed definitive CHIPS Act agreements with the US Department of Commerce, unlocking $277M in federal grants and up to $1.3B in senior secured loans tied to project milestones. Combined with January's $1.5B private raise, total committed capital reaches $3.5B to fund Round Top Mountain mining and magnet plants in Oklahoma and South Carolina.

headline: GOLD OVERTAKES US TREASURIES as World's Top Reserve Asset — ECB Confirms Historic Shift
snippet: The European Central Bank's annual reserve report confirmed gold now accounts for 27% of global official reserves, overtaking US Treasuries at 22% for the first time. Sustained buying by China, Poland, Turkey, and India reshaped reserve portfolios over the past two years, while gold's price surge amplified its share by market value.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS Flip Back to Gold in April: Poland and China Drive 17-Tonne Net Purchase
snippet: After a rare net-selling month in March, central banks returned to net purchases in April, buying 17 tonnes in aggregate. Poland led with 14 tonnes (YTD: 45t, now 30% of total reserves), while China added 8 tonnes — its largest single-month purchase since December 2024.

headline: URANIUM JUMPS 3.5% to $86/lb as Meta, Microsoft Race to Lock In Nuclear Capacity for AI
snippet: Uranium spot climbed to $86.25/lb on June 3, up 3.48%, as Big Tech's nuclear buildout added fresh demand momentum. Meta contracted for up to 7.8 GW of nuclear capacity for AI datacenter operations; Microsoft secured over 800 MW. Analysts flag a widening structural supply deficit with the forward curve pricing well above current spot.

headline: MINERAL RESOURCES Exits Manitoba Lithium JV — New Age Metals Regains Full Portfolio Control
snippet: New Age Metals (TSXV:NAM) and its subsidiary Lithium Canada Development terminated their 2022 farm-in and JV agreement with Mineral Resources Limited (ASX:MIN), allowing NAM to regain 100% of its southeastern Manitoba lithium-cesium-tantalum portfolio. The exit by one of Australia's major lithium producers signals continued caution among majors on early-stage spodumene projects.

headline: CORRECTION FINALLY ARRIVES: GoldSeek Sees Hawkish Fed Chair Fears Rattling Gold and Silver
snippet: GoldSeek's June 4 commentary ties gold and silver's latest leg lower to market unease over a potentially hawkish Fed chair nomination, noting gold shed nearly 4.6% in two weeks while silver retreated just 1% — a divergence the author views as bullish for silver. Technical support at current levels and the gold-silver ratio suggest the correction may be setting up a buy.

headline: GOLD RANGE-BOUND at $4,450: Iran Conflict Pits Safe-Haven Demand Against Rate-Hike Risk
snippet: Gold has traded a narrow $4,396–$4,917 range since late March, paralysed by competing forces: safe-haven demand from the US-Iran conflict offset by oil-price-driven inflation that keeps the Fed from cutting rates — and raises odds of a hike. Analysts now see $4,500 hardening into the new long-term support floor.

headline: 3,030 g/t GOLD: Graycliff's Shakespeare Project, Ontario Delivers High-Grade Shock
snippet: Graycliff Exploration (TSXV:GRYCF) returned 3,030 g/t gold over 1.0m from the first metallurgical test hole at its Shakespeare gold project, 84 km west of Sudbury, Ontario. Additional intercepts included 454 g/t gold over 7 metres. Company chair James Macintosh called the result "well beyond expectations."
